land.text: the Aulikara core where Cliopatria draws the Western Satraps (to 409: 207-214 of 235 cells)

predecessors.note: The page gives no predecessor (the infobox fields are blank). Cliopatria draws the Western Satraps over the whole core to 409 and the Gupta Empire from 410, so the counterpart is Cliopatria's reading, not the page's.

land.text: the Kingdom of Malava: Malwa, held under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman

successors.note: The page: "Probably the rule of the Aulikaras ended with Yashodharma" and Malwa "was then conquered by the Kalachuris of Mahishmati", with no date. No dossier yet (sa-03).

capitals.name: Dashapura (Mandsaur)
capitals.note: The page: Dashapura was "almost certainly" Yashodharman's capital; Ujjayini, once thought the capital, "has since been disproven". Coordinates are approximate (the page gives none).

correction.text: Dashapura (modern Mandsaur) and its country, the Aulikara seat; the page calls the state the "Kingdom of Dasapura" and its capital Mandsaur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Aulikara row. The infobox span is 350-545 with no area; the core is the Dashapura-Mandsaur country, the researcher's radius. Cliopatria draws this land as Western Satraps to 409, Gupta from 410 (214 of 235 cells) and Vakataka from 451 (223 cells), so the Aulikara core overlaps three Cliopatria shapes. The page says the house "was never a Gupta feudatory"; the Chhoti Sadri inscription of Malava Samvat 547 (490 CE) shows Gauri a feudatory of Adityavardhana within the Aulikara house.

correction.text: the Kingdom of Malava: Malwa, held under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Kingdom of Malava under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman ("ruled 515-545 CE"). Yashodharman's pillars claim a reach "from the neighbourhood of the (river) Lauhitya" to the Western Ocean and "from the Himalayas to mountain Mahendra" (Yashodharman page); this is a panegyric claim with no date and is not drawn. Cliopatria draws Malwa as Vakataka (464 of 611 cells) and Gupta (137) in 515-545.

region.text: Dashapura (modern Mandsaur) and its country, the Aulikara seat; the page calls the state the "Kingdom of Dasapura" and its capital Mandsaur

ledger.note: c. 350: the Aulikara house is established at Dashapura. Infobox span "350-545", with the label "350-375" beside "House of Aulikara established" (the extract could not tell which date goes with which label). The page gives no origin date; Drumavardhana, the earliest known member of the second dynasty, is "c. 5th century".

region.text: the Kingdom of Malava: Malwa, held under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman

ledger.note: c. 515: Prakashadharma defeats the Hun king Toramana and Malwa is held by the Aulikaras. "Prakashadharma defeated the Huna ruler Toramana"; his Risthal inscription is "fl. 515-516 CE" (page footnote) and Yashodharman's reign is given as 515-545. The page gives no date for the defeat; 515 is the inscription and reign-start anchor, not a dated battle.

region.text: the Kingdom of Malava: Malwa, held under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman

ledger.note: c. 545: the Aulikara rule ends. Infobox span to 545 ("Death of Yashodharman 515-545"); "Probably the rule of the Aulikaras ended with Yashodharma"; the Yashodharman page: "his short-lived empire would ultimately disintegrate between c. 530-540 AD". Malwa then fell to the Kalachuris of Mahishmati (undated).

wars.name: Prakashadharma's war against Toramana

zones.text: the Kingdom of Malava: Malwa, held under Prakashadharma and Yashodharman

wars.outcome: Prakashadharma defeated the Hun ruler Toramana and held Malwa.
wars.note: The page dates neither campaign nor battle; 515 is the Risthal inscription (fl. 515-516). The Gupta dossier carries a 496-515 contest over Eran and Kausambi with the Alchon Huns; no contest is drawn here because the Aulikara page names no ground held or taken before 515.

wars.name: Yashodharman's defeat of Mihirakula
wars.outcome: Yashodharman "defeated a Huna army and their ruler Mihirakula in 528 AD and drove them out of India".
wars.note: The Yashodharman page also says he "conquered vast territories from the Hunas and the Guptas" and names no land and no date; the Aulikara page says Yashodharman's pillars have Mihirakula paying homage to him. Narasimhagupta is named as possibly having joined the 528 defeat. No zone is drawn.

certainty.note: No border is given; the Aulikara state is named by Dashapura/Mandsaur and Malwa only, and Yashodharman's claimed empire (Brahmaputra to the Western Ocean) is a panegyric, not a frontier.

sources.title: Aulikara dynasty
sources.note: Infobox span 350-545, Kingdom of Malava, Prakashadharma and Toramana, Yashodharman 515-545, Mandsaur capital, the end.

sources.title: Yashodharman
sources.note: Reign 515-545, the 528 defeat of Mihirakula, the claimed extent, the Mandsaur inscription of 532, disintegration c. 530-540.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (the alchon-huns dossier uses "Aulikara dynasty of Malwa (Prakashadharma)" as a counterpart name and the gupta-empire dossier cites Yashodharman). Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The pages disagree with Cliopatria and the Gupta dossier on who held Malwa 410-545: Cliopatria draws Gupta (410+) and Vakataka (451+); the Aulikara page makes the Aulikaras independent ("never a Gupta feudatory"), the 532 Mandsaur inscription is Yashodharman's and Nirdosha governs the area for him. The 350 start is the infobox span (its labels are garbled in the extract); the first dated inscription on the page is 490 CE (Chhoti Sadri). The Bandhuvarman inscription (436) and the Mandsaur inscription of 404/405 are not on the page opened. The Kalachuri conquest of Malwa is undated. No ruler strip: the page dates only Prakashadharma (fl. 515-516) and Yashodharman (515-545). Gazetteer names needed: Dashapura, Mandsaur (used as a coordinate radius), Lauhitya, Mahendra (text only).
